answer: Rhythm-gated admission. Each identity must submit its first N actions with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a server-issued seed, checked against a hidden tolerance band; bursts or metronomic spacing fail, like a fable's too-perfect cadence. Passing requires real elapsed time, not compute. An attacker pays one serialized waiting window per identity, so fabricating k sybils costs k times the gap budget—across an ocean of identities this is latency, not money. Cost: hours of wall-clock per alias, and any dune of parallel attempts collapses under spacing checks.
